**Food :  AIP  9 July 2026 version**

**Evaluative questions and suggested answer by Wallace for Squid1\_1 testing**

| Where fixed wing aircraft coming to Hong Kong should first land when arrive to Hong Kong? |
| :---- |
| Hong Kong International Airport |
|  |
| Can hypersonic jet land in Hong Kong International Airport? |
| No, under Civil Aviation Ordinance Cap.312.  Unless approval is provided by the authority. |
|  |
|  Who may travel for free ? |
| Infant under 2 year old, tour conductor, security guard, national aeronautical authority |
|  |
| Do transit flights over HKFIR need to apply permit from CAD ? |
| No except that :  a) a flight by a state aircraft including military aircraft overflying the airspace above the territory of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (i.e. flights that will overfly Hong Kong territory, including the outlying islands and territorial waters); b) a flight by an aircraft carrying munitions of war; c) a flight by an aircraft carrying dangerous goods; d) a flight notified as such by the Director-General of Civil Aviation.  |
|  |
| Is VISA needed for air traveler from Vietnam? |
| Yes. it is required (GEN 1.3 \- 2.4.2) |
|  |
| If there is dead passenger on board an aircraft to Hong Kong, to which organization in Hong Kong should the pilot notify ? |
| Airport Authority |
|  |
| For import of seafood, is licence of import required? |
| No.  (GEN 1.4 \- 1.2) |
|  |
| If i have a helicopter of 2 tonnes, should it be equipped with radio equipment for ILS when flying in Hong Kong ?  |
| No need (GEN 1.4 \- 2.1) |
|  |
| What ‘VHSK’ means? |
| SEK KONG airport in Yuen long  (Gen 2.4) |
|  |
| When the twilight on 3 May starts from? |
| 05:28 (GEN2.7-2) |
|  |
| What is the work responsibility of Airport Meteorological Office (AMO) at airport? |
| The AMO serves as the meteorological watch office and maintains meteorological watch for the Hong Kong FIR and issues SIGMET information in respect of the occurrence or expected occurrence of specified en-route weather and other phenomena in the atmosphere which necessitate the issue of SIGMETs. The AMO also serves as the aerodrome meteorological office and aeronautical meteorological station for HKIA. (GEN3.5 ch2) |
|  |
| From where we can find the criteria for the issuance of special meteorological observations report ? |
| ICAO PANS-MET (Doc 10157\) para. 2.1.2 and when the crosswind components change through 20 kt. The same set of criteria is adopted for the issuance of local special report and SPECI for mean surface direction, mean surface wind speed, variation from the mean surface wind speed (gusts), prevailing visibility, runway visual range, onset/cessation/change in intensity of weather phenomena, height of base of the lowest cloud layer, and amount of cloud layer below 1 500 ft. The detailed criteria for the issuance of local special report and SPECI are provided on the Aviation Meteorological Information Dissemination System (AMIDS) (see para. 10).  (GEN 3.1 ch3.2) |
|  |
| What is the area of airport covered by the local routine weather report ? |
| In local routine reports, present weather information is representative of conditions at the aerodrome, i.e. within a radius of approximately 8 km of the aerodrome reference point. In METAR, present weather information is representa- tive of conditions at the aerodrome and, for certain specified weather phenomena, in its vicinity, i.e. the area that lies within a radius of approximately 8 km and 16 km of the aerodrome reference point. (GEN 3.1 ch 3.5) |
|  |
| How many types of alerts as provided by WTWS for airport traffic control ? |
| a) Microburst Alert – when RWY orientated wind speed loss is 30 kt or greater and accompanied by precipitation, b) Wind Shear Alert – when RWY orientated wind speed gain is 15 kt or greater, or RWY oriented wind speed loss is between 15 kt and 29 kt, or RWY oriented wind speed loss is 30 kt or greater and not accompanied by precipitation, c) Turbulence Alert – when turbulence is of a moderate or severe intensity (as expected to be experienced by a HEAVY category aircraft (GEN 3.1 ch 4.5.2) |
|  |
| Why hilltop winds is provided to pilot ？ |
| HILLTOP WINDS 9.1.1 To assist pilots in assessing possible wind changes that may be experienced during the final phase of approach under strong wind conditions, when the 2 minute mean wind measured at approximately 2 500 ft AMSL on Yi Tung Shan (primary) or Nei Lak Shan (backup) exceeds 35 kt, it will be given at the end of the Arrival ATIS (see GEN 3.5-HKO-EQ for the location of these anemometers.) e.g. ‘2500 FT ESTIMATED WIND 160 DEG 40 KT’ （GEN3.1 ch9) |
